about: The reference table of real bodies (the owner, 2026-10-21: an environment's setting names real bodies and takes their values from here; an invented body is given by its own values). Each body's values, and in `cited` the source of each, by key of `sources`. radius_km the volumetric mean radius; mass_kg its mass (its gravity at the surface is G mass / radius squared, G = `gravity_constant`); the orbit round `around`: distance_km (semi-major axis), period_days, eccentricity, inclination_deg, node_deg and periapsis_deg (on the ecliptic, with their drift a day) and mean_anomaly_deg, all at day 0 = 2000 Jan 0.0 UT; the spin: day_hours (one turn), tilt_deg (to its orbit), and where the source gives it pole_ra_deg, pole_dec_deg and meridian_deg (on the J2000 equator, its obliquity `frame_obliquity_deg`; the meridian at J2000.0), or locked_to the body whose side it keeps facing; a shining body's light: kelvin (its colour) and lux at lux_at_km from it.

sources.nasa-sun: NASA GSFC, Sun Fact Sheet (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/sunfact.html), read 2026-10-21: volumetric mean radius, mass, effective temperature (5772 K)
sources.wikipedia-sunlight: Wikipedia, Sunlight (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunlight), read 2026-10-21: the solar illuminance constant E_sc = 128 000 lux, sunlight's illuminance at Earth's mean distance (1 AU, 149597870.7 km) outside the atmosphere
sources.nasa-earth: NASA GSFC, Earth Fact Sheet (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html), read 2026-10-21: volumetric mean radius, mass, obliquity to orbit; surface pressure 1014 mb (read 2026-10-21)
sources.nasa-moon: NASA GSFC, Moon Fact Sheet (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/moonfact.html), read 2026-10-21: volumetric mean radius, mass, synchronous rotation (sidereal rotation 655.720 h = its orbit), obliquity to orbit; surface pressure (night) 3 x 10-15 bar (read 2026-10-21)
sources.nasa-mars: NASA GSFC, Mars Fact Sheet (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/marsfact.html), read 2026-10-21: volumetric mean radius, mass, obliquity to orbit; surface pressure 6.36 mb at mean radius (4.0 to 8.7 mb by season) (read 2026-10-21)
sources.schlyter: Paul Schlyter, How to compute planetary positions (stjarnhimlen.se/comp/ppcomp.html), read 2026-10-21: the orbital elements at day 0 = 2000 Jan 0.0 UT on the ecliptic and equinox of date and their drift a day (the Sun's orbit turned round to Earth's, periapsis + 180); distance_km its a (Earth's and Mars's in AU of 149597870.7 km, the Moon's in Earth radii of 6378.14 km); period_days 360 over the sum of its drifts of node, periapsis and mean anomaly (the period in that frame: Earth's 365.2422, the tropical year; NASA's sidereal 365.256, 27.3217, 686.980 differ by the equinox's precession)
sources.iau: IAU WGCCRE report 2015 (Archinal et al. 2018, Celest. Mech. Dyn. Astr. 130:22), as kept before in this repository: the north pole's right ascension and declination on the J2000 equator, the prime meridian at J2000.0 from the equator's ascending node, and its turn a day as day_hours = 24 x 360 / that turn (Earth's: the stellar day)
sources.iau-frame: IAU 1976: the obliquity of the ecliptic at J2000.0, 84381.448 arcseconds
